sections.html:
Livonia is a large suburb on Detroit's west side, with owners living in 87.2 percent of its housing. That ratio means most sales are ordinary owner-to-buyer transfers, with a smaller group of rentals that fall under a strict city licensing program.

The July 1, 2025 population estimate is 92,603, a 3.1 percent drop from the 2020 base of 95,529. Much of the housing went up in the postwar years, when the city grew quickly after becoming a city in 1950, so gather your permit history before you list. The city issues permits for additions, decks, basement finishing and similar work, and open permits or violations are tracked by the Inspection Department.

For 2020 to 2024, Livonia has high incomes and a high share of owners.

Median monthly owner costs are $1,698 with a mortgage and $678 without one. Since 92 percent of residents stayed put for a year, a house that comes up for sale has often had the same occupants for years, and buyers may expect to see original systems and finishes.

Most addresses fall in Livonia Public Schools, which runs Franklin, Churchill and Stevenson high schools. A portion of northeast Livonia is served by the Clarenceville School District. Check the district for your exact street before the listing names a school zone.

The mean trip to work is 24.3 minutes, and public bus service is limited, so households here depend on cars. Highway access and garage space are therefore worth mentioning in a listing. Buyers also ask about amenities such as the four public library locations and the community recreation center on Hubbard Road.

sections.h2: Does a Livonia rental need a license before it can be sold?
sections.html:
Livonia licenses and inspects rentals, and a rental may not be occupied without a rental license and a Certificate of Compliance. Licenses renew annually or at title transfer, and inspections happen annually, at a change of tenants or at a change of ownership, whichever comes first.

If you own a rental and plan to sell, take these steps:

  • Give the Inspection Department a copy of the purchase agreement, which lets the city cancel a renewal that was already scheduled.
  • Keep any follow-up inspection already booked so open violations get cleared.
  • Tell the buyers the city will need to inspect if violations remain after title moves.
  • After closing, the new owners take their Property Transfer Affidavit and Homestead Affidavit to the Assessor and then bring copies to the inspectors.

The city applies the state occupancy standard of 225 square feet for the first person and 70 for each additional person, not counting baths or closets. Common rental violations include dryer venting, missing smoke alarms and GFCI outlets, and a furnace carbon monoxide check every three years by a mechanical contractor. Call the Inspection Department at 734-466-2580 for the current fees and wait times, because the lead time can run about a month.

The city sends real and personal property tax bills on July 1 and December 1, so a house that closes in between usually has one bill still to be divided between buyer and seller. The summer bill's deadline is September 14. The Treasurer then splits the collections among the city, two school districts (Livonia and Clarenceville), Schoolcraft College, the state education tax, Wayne County, Wayne RESA and the Oakland ISD.

Delinquent real property taxes go to the Wayne County Treasurer. Fees for open permits, violations, vacant or abandoned property registration and Certificate of Occupancy issues never appear in the online tax lookup. Call the Inspection Department about those. Special assessment requests go by email to the Treasurer's office.

Check the city's online property inquiry before closing so your title company can see the tax history for the parcel. If the inquiry shows anything odd, call the Treasurer's office early rather than at the closing table.

sections.h2: How a Livonia deed is recorded and taxed
sections.html:
Livonia sits inside Wayne County, so the Wayne County Register of Deeds handles recording. Before recording, a deed normally needs tax certification from the county treasurer, unless an exemption applies. The register's fee schedule from January 1, 2026 lists $26 per document plus a $4 survey fee where applicable, and service is by appointment.

The state transfer tax is $3.75 for every $500 of the sale price. Wayne County charges its own levy on top, and your title company should quote the two together. Some deeds owe nothing, such as gifts to children and grandchildren.

Two deadlines start at closing. The buyer must report the transfer to the Livonia assessor within 45 days. You must cancel your homestead exemption within 90 days of moving out if you no longer qualify.

sections.h2: Choosing between a listing and a cash sale
sections.html: A traditional listing fits a Livonia house that shows well, if you can live with weeks of showings. A cash sale suits a house with open violations, a tenant, or deferred repairs. Whichever you choose, collect your deed information, the last tax bills, and any permit paperwork first. If the house was a rental, call the Inspection Department about the purchase agreement before you accept an offer. A cash buyer takes the house as it stands and does not wait on a lender. The title company then arranges the county certification and recording. Compare offers by the net you keep after taxes, recording costs and any repairs.

sections.h2: What to do in the weeks before closing
sections.html:
Begin by asking city hall what is still open on the house. Ask the Inspection Department whether any permits are still open, because a finished deck or basement with no final inspection can slow a sale. Next, check the online tax inquiry for the parcel and confirm the summer and winter bills are paid or ready to be prorated. Then call the Treasurer's office about any special assessment, which is handled by email.

If you rent the house, tell your tenants about the sale and give the buyer the lease terms. Remind the buyer that the city will need to inspect if violations remain after title moves, and that the new owners take their affidavits to the Assessor. On closing day, bring your deed information and an ID, and ask the title company for a settlement statement that lists the recording fee, the survey fee where it applies, and both transfer taxes. Keep copies of everything you sign. A record of your move date also helps when you cancel the homestead exemption, and your agent or title officer can usually supply it.

faqs.q: How many people live in Livonia?
faqs.a: The July 1, 2025 estimate is 92,603 residents. That is down 3.1 percent from the April 2020 base.

faqs.q: Who records a deed for a house in Livonia?
faqs.a: The county register of deeds, after the county treasurer certifies the taxes. Service there is by appointment.

faqs.q: When is the summer tax bill due in Livonia?
faqs.a: Billing goes out July 1 for summer, with a September 14 deadline that rolls to the next business day on weekends and holidays. Winter bills follow on December 1.

faqs.q: Does my Livonia rental need an inspection before I sell it?
faqs.a: Send the Inspection Department the purchase agreement so a scheduled inspection can be cancelled or kept to clear violations. The city inspects rentals at a change of ownership, so call 734-466-2580.
Livonia Public Schools covers most addresses and operates Franklin, Churchill and Stevenson high schools. Part of northeast Livonia belongs to Clarenceville, so look up your own street.
